observations: Art: Root inspected all60 fresh native Art PNGs through ten six-image sheets, including front/side/rear, both front quarters, rear quarter, bonnet, rear closure, pillar and overhead views. Compared against the six-model baseline sheets and the actually inspected reference photos/catalogue views.

Art: Wrangler: upper door pressing and rear returns carry a more varied highlight without separating shut lines or glazing. Open hood/cowl vents remain visible. Fog pods now show recessed dark optical bowls and small emitters rather than flat luminous coins. The factory silhouette remains simplified and the brake guides render warm under the current exposure.

Art: Bronco: broad bonnet plateau is retained with flatter outboard sections; the rear haunch and lower door draw remain continuous at oblique views. Hardtop/glass/door joints are closed in the inspected views. Factory wheel and grille fine detail remains approximate.

Art: Civic: straight principal A-pillar/seal fit is preserved in the close side view; bonnet ridges, crowned deck, wrapped end corners and formed rear recess remain coherent in front/rear/overhead views. The new rear quarter/lower door contour is subtle. Lamp construction and cabin retain simplified details.

Art: Sprinter: front cabin bow, short bonnet stamping and rounded rear roof/cabin returns are visible, with open cabin glass and continuous crew/cargo pressings. Rear door and lower body remain closed; roof ribs and fittings preserve their shape. Side windows, optics and interior are procedural approximations.

Art: HUMMER SUV: hood crest/well and vents remain readable from above; rear haunch and closure turns retain continuous side highlights. Fender/door/glass boundaries remain closed in these captures and tires sit below the open wheel arches. Tail fittings and interior remain simplified.

Art: Urus: bonnet carbon/paint domains stay separate and cooling ducts remain recessed; front wraps and hatch fold read in oblique/rear views. Fuller rear shoulder and tucked rear greenhouse keep the sloping roof silhouette. Cabin glazing stays open. Front fascia, side glass and rear fine surfacing remain below OEM/production racing-game precision.

Art: No missing body/material, new culling hole or gross intersection requiring another mesh correction was observed in this pass. This is a review of the listed views, not proof of exact photographic likeness from every camera.
Detail: Root inspected all six final Detail PNGs: meadow close/wide, winter drift wide, scanned snow close, slushy edge and snowbank scenery.

Detail: Meadow shows varied small textured tufts and low broadleaf groups over mottled ground. Large procedural blades and repeating ground patches remain visible; this pass preserves those assets and shading.

Detail: The snow close-up shows wind/granular normal detail and broad physical relief. Edges break into damp brown/white coverage, with snowbank/cliff scans and trees behind. The wide drift camera is partly occluded by a foreground pine branch; separate close and edge images still expose the snow surface. Blocky cliff silhouettes remain a known fidelity limit.
Ruts: Root inspected all 16 final rut PNGs through three sheets: oblique/profile pairs for six controlled surfaces and actual driven mud/snow.

Ruts: Firm dirt has a light shallow band. Mud and wet grass show recessed channels with broad rounded shoulders and exposed darker soil. Snow has blue compacted channels, fine tread relief and rounded displaced edges. Sand and loose dirt remain lighter and shallower. These surfaces do not show the uniform black rubber strips used on pavement.

Ruts: The actual driven Jeep mud/snow images retain grooves behind the tires, with disturbed soil or packed snow appropriate to each surface. The profile views expose rounded banks rather than tall pointed piles. These bounded profiles and 101 numerical checks do not establish unlimited excavation or deformation of the authored Winter Expedition landscape.
Transitions: Root inspected all 14 final transition PNGs in three sheets: two angles each for dirt/asphalt, mud, rock, sand, snow, wetland and mud/rock.

Transitions: Pavement retains a narrow shoulder while mud, sand and wetland break into irregular mottled ground. Snow shows a broken damp fringe with scattered bare ground, and exposed rock blends through soil patches. The surface types remain readable from the wider views.

Transitions: Some borders still read as broad color bands and ground texture patterns repeat. This pass retains those terrain materials and scene placements. Static views complement the 53 coverage/grip/rigidity checks and the separately passed 84 driving/momentum checks.
Full: Root inspected all 22 final Full PNGs through four sheets: all-six quarry tire support, six driven soil spans, crushed grass, six Urus hero directions, acceleration and open/locked climbs.

Full: The six quarry contact images show the wheels and bodies separated from the rock surface without the former gross body burial. Small gaps at individual tires reflect uneven support; numerical support/body-clearance checks provide the motion evidence.

Full: Driven firm dirt remains a faint light trail, mud/wetland show darker disturbed soil with grooves, snow shows blue compacted channels and tread detail, sand is pale, and loose dirt has shallow exposed-soil bands. The crushed-grass patch is subtle. Ground repetition and simplified vegetation remain visible.

Full: The additional six Urus hero captures are elevated staging poses, as in this fixture design; the separate settled Art images establish ordinary ride presentation. Bonnet/door/hatch material boundaries and open glazing remain coherent in the inspected views.

Full: Acceleration and open/locked rock-climb captures show the actual native HUD and obstacle contact. Static views complement the 287 passed driving/control/equipment/quarry checks; they do not alone establish an entire manual drive.
Movement: Root inspected all 13 final Movement PNGs: seven coasting terrain boundaries and all six vehicles after rounded-rise/brake trials.

Movement: The transition captures show the Jeep on the far side of each boundary at roughly 21–27 mph, with visible body clearance. Snow and uneven rock produce body roll while the chassis remains above the ground. Separate numerical checks establish momentum retention and lack of abrupt terrain impacts.

Movement: All-six rise/brake views show an upright body and ground-level tires, with pavement skid strips under the braking trials. No new gross nose burial is visible. These are end-state images; the 84 native checks provide the intervening motion and suspension evidence.
Winter: Root inspected all six final Winter PNGs: four road locations with different vehicles and elevated coast/quarry overviews.

Winter: The complete acquired scene retains icy dark road strips, ploughed snowbanks, bare shrubs, rock cliffs, blue icicles, coast water and the quarry stone wall/buildings. Vehicles appear upright on the road without visible gross body penetration in these capture poses.

Winter: The two overhead cameras expose the road and surrounding coast/quarry scenery. Static captures accompany 46 native checks, including short road-driving trials and road joins; they do not demonstrate a continuous trip over the whole road. The authored landscape and road remain static.
Presets: Root inspected all three final graphics-preset PNGs in the matched Slate Rim view: Cool, Balanced and capped Quality smoke.

Presets: Quarry rocks, trees, terrain and the Urus render in all three without an observed new missing mesh or see-through boulder. Shadow/detail differences remain consistent with the presets. The car is partly outside the lower frame in this preset camera; separate Art captures provide the body review.

Presets: The three sets of 16 numerical checks passed. Bounded telemetry peaks were 65 C Cool, 72 C Balanced and 68 C Quality smoke, below the 77 C cutoff. This does not establish normal 60 FPS endurance or long-session thermal stability.

Rollover: Root inspected all 40 final rollover PNGs across seven sheets: both flanks and roof on pavement/Pine Ridge for all six, plus four Sprinter partial rolls, after actual garage selection and activation.

Rollover: All six visibly rest on their outer side or roof structure in the inspected rolled cases; the van rear-corner/side burial from the old baseline is absent. The underside views show the opposite tires clear of the ground, and the roof-down views retain body/ground contact at their roof contour.

Rollover: The two55-degree Sprinter setups self-right under normal gravity and end upright; their positive body clearance is expected. The110-degree setups settle onto the van side. There is no imposed upright correction during the trial.

Rollover: Measured worst body-probe penetration across all 40 final cases is 0.4629 inch. Both 55-degree Sprinter setups first enter the requested physical roll and then self-right naturally. All 40 requested-pose observations and the 321 mass/contact/recovery/input checks passed. These bounded cases and images do not establish every possible terrain pose.

limits: Procedural reference-built vehicle models retain simplified interiors, optics and fine surfacing.
All six bodies are refined. Terrain shading and scene placements are retained; some ground repetition remains.
Physical ruts apply to the proving ground. Authored Winter Expedition landscape and road remain static.
Forty rollover cases and capped automated driving/image review do not establish every pose/obstacle, a manual/controller session, normal60FPS endurance or long-session thermal stability.
